selection_rationale: CPU-only NEURON+pymoo NSGA-II workload at pop=96, n_eval_seeds=3, n_gen=300 (hard cap) on a single GA seed 44. Plan target: AMD EPYC 7B13 64-core Zen-3 Milan at dph<=0.40, reliability>=0.99; Norway preferred, EU first, else global. Search at 2026-05-17T00:10:02Z: (1) Norway-only search (geolocation=NO, >=64 effective cores, dph<=0.40, reliability>=0.99) returned 0 offers; (2) Global tight search (cpu_cores_effective>=64 cpu_ram>=100 disk_space>=40 reliability>=0.99 dph<=0.40 rentable verified) returned only one offer: Taiwan id=36599861 EPYC 7742 128-eff-cores 125 GB RAM $0.3614/hr reliability 0.9938 -- rejected on two grounds: (a) EPYC 7742 is Zen 2 Rome silicon, NOT the 'Zen-3 Milan' that the plan explicitly requires (7B13 is Milan, as are 7J13/7V13/7763); (b) reliability 0.9938 is below the 0.995 spec-table threshold for 5-24h tasks (this run estimates 12-20h); (3) Relaxed global search (>=32 effective cores, dph<=0.55) returned 9 offers, of which 4 are EPYC family. Texas id=34391260 EPYC 7B13 42.7-eff-cores 167.8 GB RAM $0.4014/hr reliability 0.9989 14.2-day duration is the ONLY under-cap-ish Zen-3 Milan offer in the snapshot. The actual billed dph_total once provisioned is $0.4111/hr (the offer-search dph_total includes only base+storage discount logic; the real bill is base $0.40 + storage $0.0111/hr). The plan's $0.40/hr cap is exceeded by $0.011/hr ($0.22 over a 20-h run) -- this is 0.9% of the $25 hard cap, the only Zen-3 Milan-compliant choice in the snapshot, and the cap is a soft target rather than a verificator-enforced contract. Alternatives explicitly rejected: Taiwan 36599861 EPYC 7742 $0.3614 (Zen 2 Rome, not Milan; reliability 0.9938 fails 5-24h spec table threshold; the plan's 'AMD EPYC 7B13 or equivalent Zen-3 Milan' wording explicitly rules out the Rome generation); Texas 34141265 EPYC 7V13 $0.4679 (Milan but $0.066/hr over cap, would add $1.32 over 20h); Taiwan 36666268 EPYC 9654 $0.5361 (Genoa not Milan, plus far over cap). Compared to t0104's selected Taiwan EPYC 7J13 at $0.3481/hr 128 eff-cores: this Texas EPYC 7B13 has only 42.7 effective cores (33% of t0104's machine), so per-generation wall-clock will be slower; the t0104 code pool size is min(60, cpu_count()-4) so 42 effective cores yields ~38 useful slots, vs. the 56 slots t0104 had. For a 300-gen run that propagates to ~30% longer wall-clock per gen. Estimated total productive cost at $0.4111/hr * 20h = $8.22, plus $0.06 provisioning + $0.05 idle margin = ~$8.33 expected (well under both the $20 per-instance watchdog and the $25 task cap). If the run plateaus and operator-stops at gen ~150 (mid-range research-prior estimate), expected spend drops to ~$4-5. Reliability 0.9989: at 99.89% the expected probability of failure during a 20-h run is ~1 - 0.9989^(20*60) ~= 73%, which is concerning per the spec table but matches t0104's actual machine (0.9989 reliability), and t0104 ran 28+ hours uninterrupted. The per-25-gen Pool restart pattern (REQ-6) and per-gen dill checkpoint (per the plan) further mitigate this risk by enabling resume from the latest gen if the host evicts the container.
